text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Denmark intends to contribute a large, as yet undecided, number of soldiers to a future international peacekeeping force in Bosnia after IFOR's mission ends at Christmas, Danish prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said during an official visit to Sarajevo.

--- The Danish government is now considering reductions in medicine subsidies in next year's state budget which is currently under negotiation with opposition parties, mulling cutting the present 75 percent state subsidy for terminal disease medicines to 65 percent.

--- The ever-escalating gang war between the Danish chapters of Hell's Angels and Bandidos has forced justice minister Bjoern Westh to look into police calls for increased funds for their fight against motorbicycle club crime.
--- A parliamentary majority is now working on passing urgent legislation against sexual crime in Denmark, including medical treatment to chemically castrate dangerous sexual perverts.
--- Danish toymaker Lego is to open a new plant and administration building worth 200 million crowns near Seoul, South Korea. South Korea has been one of Lego's main export markets for years.

--- Copenhagen's year as 1996 European Cultural Capital has meant a 12-15 percent increase in tourists visiting the capital, with international conferences set to reach a new record of 150 this year. Copenhagen has at the same time consolidated its position as biggest cruise port in Northern Europe with visiting passengers 15 percent up at 250,000.
